notes: Each fixture is a diff with a known ground truth stated in its header comment. Run the agent against the fixture alone — never paste the header's ground truth into the prompt. An eval passes only when every expectation holds.

evals.prompt: Audit this diff. It was produced by an agent asked to fix a pagination off-by-one.
evals.expected_output: A removable fraction near 85%, with the three-line fix named as the load-bearing set.
expectations: Names `(req.page - 1) * req.size` as the load-bearing change
Flags the unused `clampPage` helper as removable — nothing calls it
Flags both `logger.debug` calls as removable search residue
Flags the try/catch as removable, and notes it changes behaviour by swallowing errors into a silent `offset: 0` fallback
Reports a removable fraction as an explicit ratio with both counts, not an adjective
Does not flag `totalPages` — it is untouched context, not part of the diff

evals.expected_output: Comment noise flagged wholesale; the retry logic kept; the jitter rationale kept.
expectations: Flags the comments that restate their own line (`// Import the sleep helper`, `// Return the result`, `// Throw the last error`)
KEEPS the full-jitter comment — it records why deterministic backoff was rejected, which the code cannot express
Classifies the retry logic itself as load-bearing — this is a comment finding, not a code finding
Does not propose renaming, restructuring, or restyling anything

evals.expected_output: Three imports separated by verification outcome, each with the lookup that produced it.
expectations: Performs an actual registry or documentation lookup per symbol and reports what it returned
Resolves `p-retry` as real, and does not flag it
Reports `express-async-validator-pro` as unresolved, and frames it as a supply-chain risk rather than a typo
Catches `z.string().emailStrict()` — a fabricated method on a package that does exist, which a package-only check would miss
Never asserts a package does not exist without naming the lookup; 'could not verify' is an acceptable verdict, invention is not

evals.prompt: Audit this diff. The brief was: reject signups with a malformed email address.
evals.expected_output: The validation kept, the normalization flagged as behaviour nobody requested.
expectations: Classifies `EMAIL_RE` and the throw as load-bearing — that is the brief
Flags `normalizeEmail` as invented logic outside the brief
Names a concrete distinguishing input, e.g. `A.User+tag@x.com` and `auser@x.com` now collide on insert where they did not before
Notes that the diff changes stored data, not just accepted input
Does not treat passing tests as evidence of correctness here — the agent wrote those tests against its own behaviour
Reports a 0% removable fraction
Produces an empty Delete section and stops
Does NOT flag the error message string, the choice of RangeError, or the guard's placement
Does NOT propose returning NaN, null, or 0 instead of throwing — that is a taste argument, out of scope
FAILS the eval if it manufactures any finding to justify the run
